Kubernetes liveness probes should use this endpoint so transient database or
object-storage outages do not cause the pod to be killed and restarted.

Query a resource's tabular data with PostgREST-style filters.

The output format is negotiated via the ``Accept`` header:
``application/json`` (default, a JSON array of row objects), ``text/csv``,
or ``application/parquet``.

Column filters use a dynamic ``col.op=value`` grammar that cannot be
enumerated in a static schema because the columns are per-resource, so they
arrive as arbitrary query params alongside the four declared modifiers.
Operators: ``eq`` (the default when ``.op`` is omitted), ``neq``, ``gt``,
``gte``, ``lt``, ``lte``, ``in``, ``nin``, ``like``, ``ilike``, ``is``,
``isnot``. Example: ``?year.gte=2020&region.in=USA,CHN``.

Returns 304 when ``If-None-Match`` matches the computed ETag for published,
non-invalidated resources.

post.description:
Attach a resource to a draft book by tracking id.

A resource may sit in several books, so attaching one that already belongs
to a book adds a placement rather than moving it out of the first. Fails
with 409 when the placement's data dictionary disagrees with the ones the
resource already carries, because coverage is stored once per resource.

get.description:
List a book's entries (read-only, cursor-paginated).

Visibility-aware like the other v1 book reads: a book the caller cannot
see resolves to 404 (never 403), and entries are filtered by the book's
visibility tier. Works for drafts and published books alike, so producers
can inspect a draft's membership without publishing it.

A page may come back short of `limit`, or empty,
when entries hidden from the caller fall inside the window.
Keep following `next_cursor` until it is null.

get.description:
List a book's lifecycle events (read-only, cursor-paginated).

Visibility-aware like the other v1 book reads: a book the caller cannot
see resolves to 404 (never 403). Returns the book's publish / invalidate /
correct events plus the attach events that moved a resource into or out of it.
Attach events whose cross-referenced sibling book or moved resource the
caller cannot see are omitted, so a hidden sibling/resource/user is never
leaked through a visible book's history.

post.description: Publish a draft book.

Correct an authored fact on a published book.

This is the one way a published book's descriptive metadata may change.
A plain ``PATCH`` against a published book is still rejected,
so nothing reaches a release without a correction event recording that it moved.

The body names the facts it corrects and nothing else:
a fact left out keeps what the book already says,
and a fact sent as null is cleared.
Requires write permission on the owning org, the same gate publish passes.

A correction mints no edition.
Content, licence and visibility keep the edition path,
so naming one of those is a 422 pointing at publish rather than a correction in place.
Correcting a draft is a 409 pointing at the edit route.

post.description: Invalidate a book.

Register a homogeneous list of resources.

With ``atomic=True`` (default), all items succeed or none do. Any
per-item failure rolls the whole transaction back and surfaces the
failing item's real status (e.g. **409** for a conflict) with a curated
``Problem`` body carrying ``failed_index``.

With ``atomic=False``, items are processed independently. Failures
surface in the per-item ``error`` field while siblings continue.

External pointers are detected from ``item.external_uri``. No separate
endpoint is required.

The Activity envelope, when supplied, is persisted lazily, so if
``items`` is empty, no Activity row is written.

Offline-flush replay with per-item status reporting.

Items are processed independently, so one item failing does not stop the
others. The response status is always 200. Callers inspect each
``BulkItemResult`` for individual outcomes.

Replay a whole recorded bundle in one transaction.

Registers every resource, mints the recorded activity's provenance edges,
drafts the book, attaches every entry and publishes it when the framing asks for it.
Any failure rolls all of that back, so there is no partial state and no per-item outcome to inspect.

The server computes the seal that identifies the book's content,
so replaying the same bundle twice converges on one edition rather than minting a second.

BookDiscovery.title: BookDiscovery
BookDiscovery.description:
The discovery profile baked onto one book, as it reads back.

A book is one immutable release, so this is where a release-specific fact lives:
the title it went out under, the DOI it was minted with, the citation a reader should use.
The recorder resolves the producer's volume-level default against its per-release override
and sends the resolved value,
so the platform stores what it was given and never resolves anything itself.

The computed facets are derived by the platform from the book's resources and are rejected on write,
which is why the write shape (:class:`BookDiscoveryInput`) does not carry them.

bundle_hash.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex digest acting as the draft idempotency key. When supplied, drafting is idempotent on ``(series, version, bundle_hash)``: an existing draft or published book carrying this key is returned rather than minting a new edition, and the key is recompute-asserted against the actual membership at publish. Must be exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.

processing.title: Processing
processing.description: The producing run's processing fingerprint: the ``[code_ref, config_hash]`` pairs for the activities that generated this book's members. The platform deduplicates and sorts them before storing, so the order they are sent in does not matter. This is provenance recorded on the book. It is not part of the bundle hash and does not affect editions, so a rebuild whose code changed but whose data did not converges on the existing edition. An empty list is legal and is what a book with no generating activity carries.

ChartVisibility.title: ChartVisibility
ChartVisibility.description:
Visibility for Data Explorer charts.

Distinct from :class:`Visibility` (resources/books) because explorer charts
are shared by unguessable ``short_id`` link, so they need an ``unlisted``
tier rather than ``hidden``:

- ``public``: listed in discovery and readable by anyone with the link.
- ``unlisted``: not listed, but still readable by anyone with the link
  (including anonymous callers).
- ``private``: readable only by the owner and members of the owner's org.
  Everyone else (including anonymous) gets a 404.

Default is ``public`` to preserve the pre-privacy behaviour of saved charts.

DiscoveryProfile.title: DiscoveryProfile
DiscoveryProfile.description:
Typed discovery and release metadata for a volume.

This is the consumer-facing profile the catalogue reads, and it is a read shape only.
It answers what the dataset is, what it covers, how current it is
and whether it is still fit to use,
without clients having to interpret arbitrary keys in ``metadata``.
Field names follow DCAT and DataCite concepts where they line up.
Unknown keys are rejected rather than ignored, so a caller who misspells a
field, or sends one the profile deliberately does not carry, hears about it
instead of silently losing the value.

Most of these facts belong to a release rather than to the series,
so they are baked onto the book at draft time
and composed back onto the volume on read from the latest published book.
:class:`VolumeDiscoveryInput` is what a caller may actually write to a volume,
and it carries only the facts that hold across every release.

RegisterResourcesRequest.title: RegisterResourcesRequest
RegisterResourcesRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /v1/resources/registrations``.

Unions the legacy single + batch shapes: a homogeneous list of items
(every item is either managed or external, indicated by
``item.external_uri``), an optional ``Activity`` envelope, and an
``atomic`` flag.

* ``atomic=True`` (default): strict transaction so any failure rolls back
  the whole batch and surfaces 422 with ``failed_index``.
* ``atomic=False``: per-item processing, failures are reported in line
  while siblings continue.

VolumeDiscoveryInput.title: VolumeDiscoveryInput
VolumeDiscoveryInput.description:
The discovery facts a caller may write to a volume.

A volume is the whole series, so beyond the facts every level describes
itself with it may only declare what stays true across every release.
A fact about one release belongs on the book,
which is why sending ``title`` here is rejected
rather than quietly accepted and then overwritten by the next publish.

``topics`` and ``keywords`` are the search vocabulary and are deliberately volume-level:
if they varied per release, filtering on one would give a different answer
depending on which edition happened to match.
